# @aitofy/browser-profiles

Self-hosted anti-detect browser profiles. The open-source alternative to AdsPower and Multilogin.
One package, three faces: a TypeScript library, a CLI, and an MCP server for AI agents.
npm: @aitofy/browser-profiles. License MIT. Node >= 18. Zero telemetry.

## Index

This file is the whole story in one page. The same material, split up, lives next to it:

  docs/library.md             Library API: quickLaunch, BrowserProfiles, Puppeteer, Playwright, command registry.
  docs/cli.md                 Every CLI command, alias and flag, the --json contract, keepAlive, --detached.
  docs/mcp.md                 MCP setup per client, the tools table, error shape, browser ownership.
  docs/playwright-mcp.md      Hand a wsEndpoint to Playwright MCP or any CDP client.

  docs/browser-lifecycle.md   Who owns the browser, reuse, cross-process close, detached trade-offs.
  docs/troubleshooting.md     Common failures with their exact message and the fix.
  docs/adr/0001-command-registry.md  Why one registry generates the CLI, the MCP server and the library API.
  examples/                   Runnable files: quick launch, proxy profile, Playwright, JSON pipeline, MCP.
  README.md                   Landing page. CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CHANGELOG.md as usual.

## What it does

Stores browser profiles locally (proxy, timezone, fingerprint, cookies, Chrome user data) and
launches real Chrome with anti-detect. engine=auto (the default) uses kernel mode when the
executable is fingerprint-chromium (engine-level spoof from a per-profile seed, no JavaScript
hooks) and JavaScript injection over CDP otherwise. Inject mode covers
WebRTC, Canvas, WebGL, Audio, navigator, workers, timezone, Intl locale. The user agent and Client Hints are
built from the major version of the Chrome that is actually running, read with Browser.getVersion
at launch; a pinned fingerprint.userAgent wins and logs a warning when its major differs. Kernel
mode ignores a pinned user agent so the UA stays the binary's own version. The WebGL
vendor/renderer is picked once per profile, consistent with its platform, and stored in
fingerprint.webgl (inject mode; the kernel derives the GPU from the seed). Every worker target
(dedicated, module, shared, service) runs the same spoof as the main thread. Authenticated proxies are handled by a local relay.
Profiles persist between runs, so logins survive. A profile created with fingerprint=real
(stored as fingerprint: {mode: "real"}) launches with Chrome's own identity: no engine, no user
agent or Client Hints override, no injected script, no timezone or locale change unless the
profile sets one. Use it for accounts signed in by hand; a real profile refuses engine kernel/inject.

Benchmark (docs/benchmark.md, scripts/measure.mjs): kernel mode scores 100% on browserscan and passes
a Cloudflare challenge, like AdsPower; inject mode scores 85% and creepjs flags its hooks.

## Installation

npm install @aitofy/browser-profiles rebrowser-puppeteer-core
npm install -g @aitofy/browser-profiles   # for the CLI and the MCP server

## MCP server

Start command: `browser-profiles mcp` (also installed as the bin `browser-profiles-mcp`).
Transport: stdio. Flags: --storage-path <dir>, --verbose.

Client config (Claude Desktop, Cursor, any MCP client that takes a command):

  {"mcpServers": {"browser-profiles": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@aitofy/browser-profiles", "mcp"]}}}

Claude Code one-liner:

  claude mcp add browser-profiles -- npx -y @aitofy/browser-profiles mcp

### The flow an agent should follow

1. profile_create {name: "Acme Main", id: "acme-main", proxy: "http://user:pass@host:8080"}
   -> a StoredProfile with an id.
2. browser_open {idOrName: "acme-main"}
   -> {profileId, wsEndpoint, port, pid, reused}.
3. Use wsEndpoint. It is a CDP WebSocket URL:
   - Playwright MCP: start it with --cdp-endpoint <wsEndpoint>
   - Puppeteer: puppeteer.connect({browserWSEndpoint: wsEndpoint})
   - Playwright: chromium.connectOverCDP(wsEndpoint)
   Tabs opened by that client are protected as well; the launcher re-applies the injections to
   every new page target.
4. browser_close {idOrName: "acme-main"} when done.

Calling browser_open twice for the same profile does not start a second Chrome: it returns the
running endpoint with reused: true.

### MCP tools

profile_list        List stored profiles.
                    args: groupId? (string, exact match), tag? (string, exact match)
                    out: StoredProfile[]
profile_get         Show one profile with proxy and fingerprint.
                    args: idOrName (string, required)
                    out: StoredProfile
profile_create      Create a profile with its own storage, proxy and fingerprint.
                    args: name (required), id?, proxy?, timezone?, fingerprint? ("generated" | "real"),
                          language?, platform?, tags?, notes?
                    out: StoredProfile
profile_update      Change fields of a profile; omitted fields stay as they are.
                    args: idOrName (required), name?, proxy? (null removes the proxy), timezone?,
                          fingerprint?, language?, platform?, tags?, notes?
                    out: StoredProfile
profile_delete      Delete a profile and all of its browser data. Irreversible.
                    args: idOrName (required), force? (boolean, closes a running browser first)
                    out: {id, deleted: true}
profile_duplicate   Copy a profile's settings into a new profile with a new id.
                    args: idOrName (required), name? (defaults to "<source name> (Copy)")
                    out: StoredProfile
browser_open        Open Chrome with a stored profile and return its CDP endpoint.
                    args: idOrName (required), headless? (default false), startUrl? (absolute URL),
                          detached? (default false; true = Chrome outlives the caller, reduced protection),
                          engine? ("auto" | "kernel" | "inject"; a real profile accepts only "auto")
                    out: {profileId, wsEndpoint, port, pid, reused, detached, engine}
                         engine is "kernel", "inject", or "real" (Chrome's own fingerprint)
browser_launch      Throwaway Chrome with a random fingerprint and no saved profile. Nothing persists.
                    args: proxy?, headless? (default false), randomFingerprint? (default true), detached? (default false)
                    out: {profileId, wsEndpoint, port, pid, temporary: true}
browser_close       Close the browser of a profile, from any process (reads its lock file).
                    args: idOrName (required; also accepts a tmp-... id from browser_launch)
                    out: {profileId, closed}
browser_close_all   Close every browser started from this storage path, temporary ones included.
                    args: none
                    out: {closed: string[]}
browser_status      Running browsers with their CDP endpoints. Stale lock files are cleaned up.
                    args: none
                    out: {running: [{profileId, pid, port, wsEndpoint, startedAt, temporary, engine}]}
storage_path        Directory where profiles and browser data are stored.
                    args: none
                    out: {path}

### Argument formats

idOrName    A profile id ("acme-main", or a random 16-hex-character id) or the exact profile name,
            case-insensitive ("Acme Main"). Ids are tried first. Use profile_list to discover both.
id          1-64 characters of letters, digits, hyphen or underscore. Must not already exist.
proxy       A URL with an explicit port: <scheme>://[user:pass@]host:port
            Schemes: http, https, socks5 (socks and socks5h are normalised to socks5).
            Percent-encode reserved characters in credentials: "http://bob:p%40ss@10.0.0.1:8080".
timezone    IANA id, e.g. "America/New_York". Match it to the proxy exit country.
fingerprint "generated" (default, spoofed) or "real" (Chrome's own identity, for hand-made logins).
            A real profile rejects platform. Switching to real keeps only the language and drops
            the stored timezone unless timezone is passed in the same update.
language    BCP 47 tag, e.g. "en-US", "vi-VN". Default "en-US".
platform    Exactly one of "Win32", "MacIntel", "Linux x86_64". Must agree with the user agent.
tags        Array of strings, e.g. ["facebook", "client-acme"].
notes       Free-form string stored with the profile. Not sent to the browser.
startUrl    Absolute URL opened in the first tab.

### Errors

Tools never throw. A failure comes back as an error result carrying a code and a message:
PROFILE_NOT_FOUND (the message suggests close matches), INVALID_CONFIG, CHROME_NOT_FOUND,
LAUNCH_FAILED, STORAGE_ERROR, INTERNAL.

## CLI

Command tree, with the short top-level alias in brackets. Every command accepts --json,
--storage-path <dir> and --verbose.

browser-profiles profile list [list, ls]            --group-id <id> --tag <tag>
browser-profiles profile get <idOrName> [info]
browser-profiles profile create <name> [create]     --id --proxy --timezone --fingerprint --language --platform --tags --notes
browser-profiles profile update <idOrName> [update] --name --proxy --timezone --fingerprint --language --platform --tags --notes
browser-profiles profile delete <idOrName> [delete, rm]  --force
browser-profiles profile duplicate <idOrName> [duplicate] --name
browser-profiles browser open <idOrName> [open]     --headless --start-url <url> --detached --engine
browser-profiles browser launch [launch]            --proxy --headless --no-random-fingerprint --detached
browser-profiles browser close <idOrName> [close]
browser-profiles browser close-all [close-all]
browser-profiles browser status [status, ps]
browser-profiles storage path [path]
browser-profiles mcp                                --storage-path <dir> --verbose

--tags can be repeated or take a comma-separated list. --json prints exactly the command output
object on stdout, nothing else, so it can be piped into jq. On failure the CLI writes
{"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}} to stderr and exits non-zero.

Example pipeline:

  browser-profiles create "Acme Main" --id acme-main --proxy http://user:pass@proxy.com:8080 --json
  sleep 300 | browser-profiles open acme-main --json >/tmp/open.json &   # keeps stdin open
  WS=$(jq -r .wsEndpoint /tmp/open.json)
  npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --cdp-endpoint "$WS"
  browser-profiles close acme-main

## Configuration

Storage path precedence: --storage-path <dir> > BROWSER_PROFILES_HOME > ~/.aitofy/browser-profiles.
On Windows the default is C:\Users\<user>\.aitofy\browser-profiles.

Diagnostics go to stderr only, so stdout stays clean for --json and for the MCP stdio protocol.
They are silent unless DEBUG=browser-profiles* is set or --verbose is passed.

## Browser lifecycle

The process that launches Chrome owns it: the authenticated-proxy relay and the anti-detect
injections live there.
- MCP server: browser_open returns immediately, the server keeps the browser protected while it
  runs, and closes every browser it opened when it exits. A browser it only reused (reused: true)
  belongs to another process and is left running.
- CLI: browser open and browser launch print the endpoint and then stay in the foreground so the
  browser keeps its protection. Ctrl+C, SIGTERM, or the CLI's stdin closing closes the browser and
  exits. In a script, background it with a stdin that stays open, or read the endpoint from
  browser_status instead.
- detached opts out: CLI --detached, MCP detached: true, library profiles.launch(id, {detached: true}).
  Chrome outlives the caller. Inject mode keeps flag-level protection only, no authenticated-proxy
  relay, injections on the first tab only. Kernel mode keeps the spoof (it is a process flag); the
  relay limit is the same. Use for one-shot scripts: browser-profiles open acme --detached --json.
- browser_close / browser close works from any process by reading the profile lock file.

## Library API

Everything below is imported from '@aitofy/browser-profiles'.

quickLaunch({proxy, timezone, fingerprint})   Launch an anti-detect browser, no saved profile.
                                              Returns {browser, page, close}.
withPuppeteer({profile})                      Launch a stored profile and connect Puppeteer.
withPlaywright({profile})                     Same for Playwright ('@aitofy/browser-profiles/playwright').
createSession({temporary, randomFingerprint}) Throwaway session with a random fingerprint.
patchPage(page, options)                      Apply anti-detect patches to a page you already have.
generateFingerprint(options)                  Build a consistent random fingerprint.
getFingerprintScripts(fingerprint)            Injection scripts for that fingerprint.
getAllProtectionScripts(options)              The full bundle: webrtc, canvas, webgl, audio,
                                              navigator, workers.
getProfileProtectionScripts(fingerprint)      That bundle for a profile fingerprint. The launcher
                                              and both integrations inject exactly this.
createWebGLScript({vendor, renderer})         WebGL spoof for one GPU, stable across page loads.
createWorkerSpoofScript(prelude)              Wrap Worker/SharedWorker to run the prelude first.
pickWebGLForPlatform(platform)                A GPU consistent with that navigator.platform.
buildUserAgent(platform, major)               Reduced Chrome UA. buildBrands(major) for Sec-CH-UA.
buildUserAgentMetadata(platform, version)     Payload for Network.setUserAgentOverride.
parseChromeVersion(text)                      Version out of a UA or a Browser.getVersion product.
resolveUserAgent(pinned, platform, running)   {userAgent, version, mismatch}.
launchChromeStandalone(options)               Launch Chrome with no profile management.
parseProxyUrl(url) / formatProxyUrl(config)   Proxy URL <-> ProxyConfig.
createLogger(namespace)                       stderr logger used by the package.

BrowserProfiles class:
  new BrowserProfiles({storagePath?, chromePath?, defaultTimezone?, defaultProxy?})
  create(config), get(id), getByName(name), getByIdOrName(idOrName), list(options?),
  update(id, updates), delete(id), duplicate(id, name?), export(id), import(json),
  launch(id, options?), launchByName(name, options?), launchByIdOrName(idOrName, options?),
  close(id), closeAll(), createGroup(name, description?), moveToGroup(id, groupId), listGroups()

Command registry (the same definitions the CLI and MCP are generated from):
  createCommandContext({storagePath?, verbose?}), getCommand('browser.open'), commands,
  runCommand(ctx, def, input) -> Result<O, BrowserError>, resolveStoragePath(explicit?)

Commands return a Result ({ok: true, data} or {ok: false, error}) and never throw.

Minimal library example:

  import { BrowserProfiles } from '@aitofy/browser-profiles';
  const profiles = new BrowserProfiles();
  const profile = await profiles.create({ name: 'Acme Main', timezone: 'America/New_York' });
  const { wsEndpoint, close } = await profiles.launch(profile.id);
  await close();

## Use cases

Multi-account management, web scraping behind rotating proxies, testing with different browser
configurations, and letting an AI agent run isolated browser sessions through MCP.
